title: Projection normalization and thick isomorphism locus of the derived scalar mate
statement:
Let $f:Z\to T$ be a morphism of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $a_T:A_T\to B_T$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings and put $A_Z=f^{-1}A_T$, $B_Z=f^{-1}B_T$, $a_Z=f^{-1}a_T$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(A_V),D(B_V)$ of module sheaves, equivalently internal module objects [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Write $r_V:D(B_V)\to D(A_V)$ for exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], $T_V=B_V\otimes^L_{A_V}-$ for ordinary K-flat derived scalar extension with its representative-normalized adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], and $f_R^*\dashv Rf_{*,R}$ for the canonical derived module adjunctions, $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $\lambda_f:f_B^*T_T\xrightarrow{\sim}T_Zf_A^*$ be the canonical balanced pullback/tensor comparison [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. For $K\in D(A_Z)$ define $\beta_{f,K}:T_TRf_{*,A}K\to Rf_{*,B}T_ZK$ by the adjunct
$$T_Z(\varepsilon^A_{f,K})\circ\lambda_{f,Rf_{*,A}K}.$$

Use the signed-total derived tensor presentations on flat K-flat representatives [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model]. Under the canonical tensor-symmetry identification $r_VT_VM\cong M\otimes^L_{A_V}r_VB_V$ and the adjunction-compatible comparison $r_TRf_{*,B}\cong Rf_{*,A}r_Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], the restricted arrow $r_T(\beta_{f,K})$ is exactly the projection morphism
$$\pi_{K,r_TB_T}:Rf_{*,A}K\otimes^L_{A_T}r_TB_T\longrightarrow Rf_{*,A}(K\otimes^L_{A_Z}f_A^*(r_TB_T))$$
[def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-map]. With the canonical unit/counit-compatible shifts, this restricted natural transformation is between exact functors and commutes with shifts, hence gives morphisms of distinguished triangles including their connecting arrows [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The full subcategory $\{K\mid\beta_{f,K}\text{ is an isomorphism}\}$ is thick: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts, finite sums, cones and retracts. More precisely, put $F=T_TRf_{*,A}$ and $H=Rf_{*,B}T_Z$. For $K\xrightarrow{i}G\xrightarrow{r}K$ with $ri=1_K$ and $\beta_{f,G}$ invertible, the inverse of $\beta_{f,K}$ is $F(r)\circ\beta_{f,G}^{-1}\circ H(i)$. No flatness, boundedness, constructibility or invertibility of a projection formula is assumed.

proof.text: Restriction reflects derived isomorphisms by the ring-sheaf adjunction comparison. Hence locus equals the isoLocus of the restricted natural transformation. The proved source-library isoLocus instance gives its triangulated structure by zero, the shift equation and the triangle-isomorphism lemma; its retract instance and isomorphism invariance hold for any natural transformation. Transport these instances across the equality of object properties. A triangulated isomorphism-invariant property is closed under finite products; apply it to the limiting fan of the finite biproduct, including the empty family.

proof.text: For a split retract i:K -> G, r:G -> K, the explicit candidate inverse is H(i) followed by beta_G inverse followed by F(r). In its composite with beta_K, use naturality at r to cancel beta_G inverse against beta_G, then use H(i r)=1. In the other order use naturality at i and F(i r)=1. Construct IsIso from these two identities and retain both as the final conjunct. This uses only naturality and functoriality.

No SGA source; all quoted Stacks tags exist with the stated labels (06YY, 06YU, 07A4, 03EL, 0G7E, 07A6, 0A8D, 0FPT, 014A). The statement is true; tested cases: K=0, f=id, a=id, nonflat Z->Z/2, B=0, and a split retract. Step 1: e_V comes from change-of-rings-tensor-comparison plus a symmetry with no sign (coefficient in degree 0), using one K-flat factor and the resolving equivalence; it does not assume r_V B_V is K-flat. Step 2: domains checked, and U(r_T B_T) = r_Z B_Z in the identified-coefficient case. Both composites send f^{-1}(s⊗x) to f^{-1}x⊗f^{-1}s, where lambda = Q(chi) = theta^{-1} per the kflat-normalization node. mu's chain formula is implicit in the cited node, which is acceptable. Step 3, recomputed: the ring-sheaf-change-adjunction compatibility plus naturality of e_Z and step 2 give (eps⊗1)mu, whose adjunct is the pi of ringed-projection-first-shift, so R(e_Z) d r_T(beta) = pi e_T. Step 4: the shift square of d reduces to b's square by adjunction and the uniqueness of adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique. Step 5: the connecting square is explicit and uses the first-variable pi shift. Steps 6-8: conservativity, zero, shifts, sums, 2-of-3 via triangle-morphism-iso, and the retract inverse formula all verified. Advisory: step 2 overlaps lem-sfb-internal-scalar-mate-projection, which covers only the condensed special case, so it is not a duplicate. The step 2 and step 5 source fields mix two .tex files in one place string, which is cosmetic.
